message:
a133/a134/a135: the sources are 8-bit, an A/B must prove its arms differ, and the ordering clamp lands

a133 — REPLY02 §4 asked whether a99's float depth ingest is actually live on
the plate path, because if the plate is built from an 8-bit source the
fold-correct step over-flattens by construction and can never win. Two
separable questions the arc had been conflating; both now answered.

  CONTAINER  all four suite depth maps are 8-bit greyscale PNGs, read straight
             out of the IHDR with no renderer involved:
               defaultImgDepth.png     851x1023   bitDepth=8
               starwatcher_depth.png   1920x1323  bitDepth=8
               silverwarrior_depth.png 3000x3000  bitDepth=8
               roomDepth1.png          2047x1362  bitDepth=8
  DECODER    live and correct. Handed a synthesised 16-bit PNG (the same troll
             data x257, adding no information) it logs "a99: depth read at
             16-bit precision" — and a89 STILL detects a 1/255 quantum, with
             256 distinct 16-bit levels sampled and 0 samples off the 8-bit
             grid. a89 measures the information, not the container.

So the larger finding is the real one: the source is 8-bit UPSTREAM of the
ingest. The a128 result stands and is now explained rather than observed, and
it is explicitly contingent — a genuinely >=16-bit depth source would move it,
and modern estimators emit float natively.

New printed line, so nobody re-derives this from a bake log:
  a133 precision budget: geometry needs 0.00176 depth (= 0.45 source quanta,
  ~569 levels); source has 1/255.  <-- THE SOURCE CANNOT EXPRESS IT: a
  fold-correct plate step is 2.23x finer than one quantum, so enforcing it
  FLATTENS. A 569-level depth source (>= 16-bit) is what would change this.

a133b — fgTearStep in the units that matter (log only, REPLY02 §3):
  fgTearStep = 0.0600 depth = 34 px of reveal at the rim; the reveal-benefit
  gate (1px) would be 0.00176 depth, 34x lower.
Independently reproduces REPLY02's 34 px from the shipped constant and the live
k. NOT changed: a117 measured what aggressive tearing does with no plate to
back it. Complete the plate first, then lower this.

a134 — harness/abguard.js. An A/B must prove its arms diverge DOWNSTREAM of the
flag before its numbers are read, by a witness taken from inside the code path
under test — not by logging the flag's value, which only proves the assignment
happened. Two dead flags in two sessions (_coneWide into a load-time const;
_legacyPlateStep which does not exist) both produced full tables of identical
numbers, because a dead flag and a null result are indistinguishable in the
output. Wired into combstep.js and orderclamp.js; the guard voids the run and
prints no table.

a135 — THE ORDERING CLAMP (brief §4.4, promoted by REPLY02 §7).
    d_hidden(x) >= d_occluder_silhouette(x) + eps
One unconditional O(N) pass over the final plate depth. eps is DERIVED: one
source quantum, the smallest step the data can express (a89 measures it). That
lands on 0.00392 — essentially the 0.004 a43 reached empirically and that has
sat hardcoded in three places since. The magic number was measuring this.

Measured, troll, two populations counted separately because lumping them
reports 88% and means nothing:
  7401 texels (0.85%) were STRICTLY IN FRONT of the surface they back, worst by
  0.1511 depth = 38.5 quanta = 86 px of misplacement at the rim.
  A further 761836 sat flush with the source and took the eps setback only.

Pass criteria from the brief, all met:
  deg     d black    d combX    d combY
    0       0.00     -0.007     -0.009
   15      -0.01     -0.016     -0.010
   25      -0.04     -0.008     -0.007
   32      -0.02     -0.004     -0.002
   38      -0.02     -0.010     -0.004
black% unchanged-to-slightly-better, comb better on both axes at every pose.
The invariant that A21, A41, A43, A112, the backstop sweep, the cap cards and
the -0.004 push-back all exist to hunt or paper over now holds by construction.
window._noOrderClamp reverts.

regress.js masks: ALL PASS (8).
